newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean Prime Minister says willing to resign.
newsitem.headline: South Korean Prime Minister says willing to resign.

text.p: South Korean Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung is ready to resign to take responsibility for a loan scandal involving the failed Hanbo Steel Co, an official at Lee's office said on Wednesday.
"He is willing," the official, who declined to be named, said by telephone. "But it's up to the president."
"I don't think he will resign, but he has said that as prime minister he should shoulder the responsibility," the official added.
Yonhap news agency quoted an unnamed source as saying Lee told a cabinet meeting on Tuesday he was "objectively" considering his position.
"Watchers say Yi's remarks suggest that a mass resignation of the entire cabinet could follow the conclusion of the Hanbo investigation," it said.
Earlier, the official at the prime minister's office said President Kim Young-sam accepted the resignation of Home Affairs Minister Kim Woo-suk who was being probed over the scandal.
